module_title: Important Modern Books - Popular and Frequently Tested Works
introduction: Modern books, political memoirs, and celebrity autobiographies are heavily tested in the 'Books and Authors' section of Static GK. This level covers the most standard, high-frequency modern books written by notable Indian politicians, athletes, and celebrated authors that appear repeatedly in SSC, Railways, and state-level exams.

core_concepts.title: An Era of Darkness
core_concepts.description: Written by Dr. Shashi Tharoor, this widely read book explores the economic and social exploitation of India under the British Empire. It won him the Sahitya Akademi Award.

core_concepts.title: The God of Small Things
core_concepts.description: Arundhati Roy's debut novel which won the 1997 Booker Prize. Her victory was a historic moment, making her the first Indian citizen to win the prestigious award.

core_concepts.title: A Century is Not Enough
core_concepts.description: The highly popular autobiography of former Indian cricket team captain and former BCCI President, Sourav Ganguly. It chronicles his tumultuous cricketing journey and leadership.

core_concepts.title: The White Tiger
core_concepts.description: Aravind Adiga's Booker Prize-winning novel (2008). It provides a darkly humorous perspective on India's class struggle and economic disparity, narrated by a village boy who becomes a chauffeur.

important_entities.name: Dr. Shashi Tharoor
important_entities.key_fact: Books: An Era of Darkness, The Paradoxical Prime Minister.
important_entities.significance: A prominent Indian diplomat and politician famous for his extensive vocabulary and political-historical writings.

important_entities.name: Arundhati Roy
important_entities.key_fact: Books: The God of Small Things, The Ministry of Utmost Happiness.
important_entities.significance: A Booker Prize-winning author and vocal political activist.

important_entities.name: Salman Rushdie
important_entities.key_fact: Books: Midnight's Children, The Satanic Verses, Victory City.
important_entities.significance: A globally renowned British-Indian novelist. His book 'Midnight's Children' won the 'Booker of Bookers' (the best novel to have won the prize).

important_entities.name: Chetan Bhagat
important_entities.key_fact: Books: Two States, Half Girlfriend, The 3 Mistakes of My Life.
important_entities.significance: India's highest-selling English-language novelist, whose books frequently inspire Bollywood adaptations.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants often get confused between 'An Era of Darkness' and 'Inglorious Empire'. They are the exact same book—it was published as 'An Era of Darkness' in India and as 'Inglorious Empire' in the UK and US.

Do not assume that 'A Century is Not Enough' was written by Sachin Tendulkar just because he scored 100 centuries. Sachin's autobiography is 'Playing It My Way', while this book belongs to Sourav Ganguly.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: For Dada, a Century is never enough
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Connect the ambitious title directly to Sourav Ganguly's aggressive playing style.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: The God of Small Things brought Roy a 'Royal' Booker
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Associate Roy (Royal) with The God of Small Things and the Booker Prize.

exam_strategy_tips: 'Match the Following' questions involving prominent modern authors or politicians are incredibly common in SSC CGL Tier 1. Keep a consolidated list of celebrity books handy.
